# Psalm 56 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For-the-choirmaster. Upon Yonath-Elem-Rechokim [Dove-of-Distant-Silences]. Of-David. A-Miktam, when the-Philistines seized-him in-Gath.

**2** Be-gracious to-me, O-God, for man tramples-me; all the-day fighting he-oppresses-me.

**3** My-enemies trample-me all the-day, for many fight against-me, O-Most-High.

**4** [On] the-day I-am-afraid, I trust in-You.

**5** In-God — I-praise His-word — in-God I-trust; I-will-not fear. What can-flesh do to-me?

**6** All the-day they-twist my-words; against-me all their-thoughts [are] for-evil.

**7** They-stir-up-strife, they-lurk; they watch my-steps, as they-wait for-my-soul.

**8** For-[their]-iniquity — escape for-them? In-anger bring-down the-peoples, O-God.

**9** My-wanderings You-have-counted; put my-tears in-Your-bottle. [Are they] not in-Your-book?

**10** Then my-enemies turn-back in-the-day I-call; this I-know — that God [is] for-me.

**11** In-God — I-praise His-word; in-YHWH — I-praise His-word.

**12** In-God I-trust; I-will-not fear. What can-man do to-me?

**13** Upon-me, O-God, [are] Your-vows; I-will-render thank-offerings to-You.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **56:9**: 'Put my tears in Your bottle' — one of the most intimate images in Scripture. God collects and preserves human tears. No grief is wasted.

— EMET
